title: Ladybird is now in alpha
why_read: A from-scratch browser engine reaching alpha is a genuinely rare and technically significant milestone worth engineers' attention.
analysis: Ladybird is an independent web browser engine built without relying on existing codebases like Blink or WebKit. Reaching alpha means it can now render a meaningful subset of real-world websites, which is a major undertaking given the complexity of HTML, CSS, and JS standards. This matters because browser engine diversity has shrunk dramatically, and a credible new independent implementation is technically and strategically notable. Worth reading for engineers interested in browser internals or standards compliance challenges.
